(In the absence of the jury)
I'm grateful for the time, my Lord, thank you.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: Not at all, Mr Myers.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Just before the jury come into court, if I could address everyone through you, Mr Driver. The court has been made aware by a Mr Nigel Bunyan of a request, which is, in short terms, to allow the provision of an additional camera angle so that those members of the media, relatives, police officers, et cetera, who are not physically in court 7 are given a constant view/audio feed of the well of the court/dock area.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: This is an issue relating to what can and can't be seen remotely because, of course, any transmission of any part of the proceedings here is hampered by the fact that one is not in the courtroom itself. And as anyone in this court knows, all sorts of things go on in a courtroom that can't be captured by everything and cameras.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: I'm very aware of the difficulties caused by the limited space in this courtroom and the need to broadcast the proceedings to other places -- and there are a lot of broadcasts that have had to be facilitated in this case, so it is not just simply
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: transmitting it to one other place and making arrangements in relation to that. I'm also very much aware of the application of the principle of open justice and insofar as the proceedings can be open to all members of the public who want to be here, they should be open to them.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: But I'm afraid I cannot accede to the request that is made because it is just not technologically possible to do that. We have exhausted now all the technological possibilities so far as that is concerned.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: But what I will do is ensure that after the jury has left court, the camera, which will not obviously cover the jury as they are coming in and out of court, will be left on or will be activated to cover the well of the court after the jury has left court and will remain on until the defendant has left the courtroom. I can do no more than that.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: I'm not going to go into the whys and wherefores of this request. There is a limited number of spaces available for members of the media. From the outset those spaces have been allocated and known who they are allocated to. I can't engage in a process of permitting others now to come in and take places. So that's that.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Thank you for that information.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: I know that -- well, I hope Mr Bunyan is here remotely to hear that. If not, he can be told what I have said. But I will endeavour to ensure that as much as can be broadcast will be broadcast to those remote locations that are linked into this courtroom.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Thank you for the information.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: (In the presence of the jury)

As your Lordship knows, we are now going to call evidence in relation to [Baby M]. I have given Mr Stansfield copies for the jury and Mr Worthington a copy for your Lordship of some of the documents that we will consider most frequently during this chapter of the evidence. They should be housed behind divider 16 in the second file, file number 2.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: (Handed)
May I recall Mrs Mary Griffith, please.
MRS MARY GRIFFITH (recalled)
Examination-in-chief by MR DRIVER
Can I invite you to state your full name for the recording, please?
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: Mary Griffith.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: You were with us recently -- I think Thursday, 16 February -- when you gave evidence principally about [Baby L]. We've invited you back today to give evidence in relation to his brother, [Baby M].
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: From time to time, during your evidence, I'll ask you to look at some paper documents and they are in that file in front of you, the file marked number 2 down the spine and indeed behind divider 16. It might assist you if you could go there now. We will put them on the screen as well.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: When you were with us last week, you confirmed that you were working a day shift on 9 April 2016.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: On that shift, you were given the responsibility of caring for the twins [Baby L] and [Baby M]?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: They were in nursery room 1?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: Which we understand is usually the intensive care nursery?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: But from your recollection, and having had chance to remind yourself of your statement and some of the original documents last week, it's right, isn't it, that they were not designated as intensive care babies as such?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: No, all babies came into nursery 1 for admission, were stabilised, and then moved on if there was room in the other nurseries.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: Yes. You told us previously a little of your experience and your own banding as a nurse at this point in time.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: And I think from refreshing my memory of the notes, you were a band 5 nurse?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: And as a band 5 nurse would you look after intensive care babies or not?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Not all of them, no, because I hadn't done the intensive care course.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: Thank you. Can you recall where and how they were placed, how they were housed within --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: -- nursery 1? Can you remind us of that, please?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: [Baby M] was across the corner and his brother was down the back wall.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: Thank you. You made a record of various observations and various cares you provided to [Baby M], our focus this afternoon, contemporaneously and then summarised them at the end of what proves to be quite a late and long shift within your nursing notes; is that correct?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: Let's start with the original and then look at the nursing notes in due course. If you would go to that paper bundle, it might help you to take it out of the file, it's entirely up to you, they are joined together by a treasury tag — they are not, I'm told. All right.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Let's turn two pages and look at the observation chart. Thank you. Do you recognise your initials just over halfway to the right on the bottom of that page?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: If we run our eye up the page, we will see that that corresponds, unsurprisingly, to entries at 08.30 that morning.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: (Pause)
An iPad issue.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: (Pause)
Do you have the tile number for this?
Tile 84.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: Tile 84 if you wanted to look at it on your iPads.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: (Pause)
Tile number 84, please, Mr Murphy.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: There we now have on screen, Mrs Griffith, the production of the document that we have in our paper bundle and that is in the witness box before you.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: We can see, is this right, your initials corresponding to observations made initially at 08.30 and at 10.30 that morning?
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: Could you just assist us with the observations? Was there anything of note insofar as the temperature observations?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Um... No, they were fine then. They went up at lunchtime.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: The lunchtime observation that you're referring to, is that an observation made by you or initialled [Initials of Nurse B]?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: No, I was at lunch. It was [Nurse B].
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: Thank you. We'll come to the circumstances in which [Nurse B] stepped in, as it were, during your lunch break.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: The respiration readings for 8.30 and 10.30, anything of note?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: No. A bit raised, but that could have been just because he was unsettled or I was doing something with him but nothing too concerning.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: And moving up the page, the heart rate within that same time period?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: No, nothing too concerning there.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: Sorry, am I looking at the same document?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: 8.30 and 10.30, the respiration rate, you say is a bit raised. Are they --
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Sorry, it's the heart rate that was a bit raised.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: Sorry, the respirations are -- sorry.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: Well...
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: We're looking at J18782 in the bottom right corner.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: Exactly, just over halfway across.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Because although it says in the top left-hand corner "Date 8/4/16", and we get to 24.00 hours, obviously it's the 9th from then on. So we come along, over the halfway mark across to 8.30 and 10.30 --
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: -- and we can there see the readings down those columns.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: Do you have that?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: When you say "a little raised", Mrs Griffith, above which line?
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: It's the heart rate that's raised a bit. As you can see, it's been quite stationary and it goes up a bit.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: But that can happen if you're handling a baby for a feed or a nappy change. Nothing grossly worrying though.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: Thank you. The peak of it in that little undulation there appears to be before your shift, do you agree --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: -- more or less on the line that would divide 06.00 and 08.30 hours?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: Then it dips back, heading towards its former position during your watch; would you agree with that?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: Thank you. If we could then, please, look at the feeding chart for the corresponding period. Mr Murphy, that's behind
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: tile 85. On our paper document it's towards the back of the bundle at J18866 in the bottom right corner. Do you have that?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: Thank you very much. There again do we see your initials, just on this occasion, left of centre on this document?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: Thank you. Does that correspond to, again, 08.30 and 10.30 that morning?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: In summary, at 08.30 what feed did you provide to [Baby M]?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: 10ml.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: Was that 10 millilitres via a bottle?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: I can't remember, but it says B, so yes, I think it was bottle.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: And is that your shorthand for bottle?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: Corresponding to the route line?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: Bottle as opposed to NGT. That took him to a total of 37 in terms of this document.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Then again, at 10.30, it's a little more difficult to read on paper, but if Mr Murphy can help us by magnifying the corresponding image on the screen. It's there where the cursor is pointing. It appears to have been an entry crossed out and then perhaps corrected; can you see that?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: Let's take it in stages. Route, is that NGT?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: Quantity?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: 11ml.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: Thank you. So that's the, if I may say so, slightly messy digits immediately below NG; is that right?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: Taking his total to 48, 37 plus 11 is 48. Then the next entry I'm interested in where it appears to read "3.9 pre-feed"; is that right?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: Does that correspond with your handwritten entry in the left column?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: What does that inform us of?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: That's his blood sugar pre-feed.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: Is that part of the standard monitoring regime to take a neonate's blood sugar reading before at least some, if not all, of the feeds?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: To see what, if any, progress the baby is making in that regard? Is that the picture?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: Thank you very much. If we could go, please, on the screen to tile 91. We don't have this in paper form, Mrs Griffith, but this is going to be your nursing notes, I hope. There we have notes created by you at 20.11, so at the end of the shift.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: A delayed end of the shift, as it transpires to be.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: That records, does it, the fact that you took over care at 07.45, that you made all the checks necessary?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: And at that point, he, [Baby M], was self-ventilating in air, his observations were stable and satisfactory, you recorded the feeds that had been given and tolerated and the fact that,
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: because of that, the quantity was being incrementally increased; is that right?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes. The volumes increase from their age.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: Thank you. And this was his second day of life, wasn't it?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: Bloods taken to check for bilirubin and blood glucose at 10.30, and I think that's the entry that we've just seen --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: -- the pre-feed blood sugar level:
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: "Bilirubin line not below 50, so existing phototherapy was continued."
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: You confirm -- we just looked at it in manuscript -- the 3.9 blood sugar reading. Then:
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: "One small posset at 11 am."
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Was that of any note at all?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: No, it was only a small posset with wind, more or less, yes.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: And that goes with the territory, I imagine?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, can do, yes.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: Thank you. Then you made this entry:
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: "At 12.15 noted that his stomach was a little distended and his work of breathing was increased."
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: If we look at the next sentence, you were then sent for your break and your colleague, [Nurse B], did the 12.30 feed and found that his temperature was raised and she -- and she'll tell us about this in due course -- aspirated 5 millilitres of stomach acid with partly digested milk, which was discarded and the feed was given.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: So it follows from that, and could you confirm, that during this -- at this point in time, whilst you were having a break, you handed over [Baby M] to your colleague, [Nurse B]?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: Was that simply to enable you to have a break or was that because of a change in his presentation?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: No, it was to enable me to have a break.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: Thank you. You returned from your break at 1 o'clock, something like that?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, it would have been 1 o'clock, yes.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: At that point, do you recall, was there any change in the baby or the treatment or cares being given to the baby?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: No, I was told he'd settled and his temperature had come back down.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: Thank you. When would he have been fed next, can you recall?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: He was being two-hourly fed, so it would have been half past 2.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: Right. 10.30 by you, 12.30 by [Nurse B] and then 14.30 by you again, and if we look at our page J18866, can we see another -- sorry, Mr Murphy, could we get that on the screen again? That was the document behind tile 85.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Now at 14.30, I think we can see your initials, but you've put them on a different line on this occasion, can you see, a little higher up --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: -- corresponding to the millilitres per kilo hour?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, that should be further down. That is my signature.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: They are your initials? Good. If Mr Murphy could magnify that for us so we can all see it as clearly as possible. Thank you.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: To the left we have your last entry that we looked at, which included the 3.9 blood sugar reading, then we have an entry that was made during your lunch --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: -- by [Nurse B] and then your entry here. So looking at your first entry, NBM, nil by mouth?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: Do you recall why [Baby M] was now nil by mouth?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, I'd aspirated bile pre-feed.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: Thank you. Let's look down the page to see whether that's been recorded. Is that your entry?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: You tell us what it reads, is it bile?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Bile stained, I think.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: Bile stained. Then right next to the cursor, 1.5?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes. 1.5ml, yes.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: So does that reflect --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: -- your recollection that at this point in time, you having aspirated 1.5ml of bile-stained aspirate, it was decided that there would be a change in the feeding regime?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: Do you recall who made that decision?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: It would have been one of the doctors. Which doctor I don't remember.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: You can't recall. But as a matter of practice, you, having aspirated 1.5ml of bile-stained aspirate, that would be reported to a medic?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: And we will see a corresponding note to that effect in due course.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: If we look at the next entry, it bears your initial on the same line there. Looking at our paper version, if we glance up the page, we would see that corresponds to 15.30?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: Just staying with our fluid balance chart for a moment, at 15.30 we can see the digits 5.3ml per hour.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: What does that inform us of?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: An intravenous infusion of 10% dextrose.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: Thank you. So those two entries should be read together?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: Where it says 10% dextrose, 75/kg, and that is the rate of the infusion, is it?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: That's the rate of the infusion per hour, yes.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: Per hour. Thank you very much. If we go down that column for 15.30, I think that is the only entry that you made at that point.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: Does that reflect the fact that because of the aspirated bile-stained 1.5ml, he remained nil by mouth --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: -- and was receiving his nourishment --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Via the drip, yes.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: -- via dextrose, via the drip.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: The next column at 16.00, an entry by, again, your colleague [Nurse B], tells us that things changed dramatically at this point and [Baby M] was transferred to the ITU chart. So what I would like you to do now is to consider the events leading up to the change.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: If we could, please, Mr Murphy, begin this phase by going to tile 130 and look at the tile itself, please, Mr Murphy, which informs us that at 15.34 -- and if we look at the next tile because they are something of a pair, at 15.35 medication was given to [Baby L], not [Baby M] but to his brother, and that, the next tile, fluids were given to [Baby L] at 15.40. So that's really just to orientate ourselves in terms of time.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: We'll all remember your evidence from last week about how you were interrupted in attempting to hang a bag for [Baby L] by the events from his brother's cot.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: We can see that if we click on, please, to 131, for example. If we look closely at these documents, as the tile suggests, the computer record reflects that both you and your colleague Lucy Letby were involved in this process. Does that accord with your memory?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: We've asked this of many witnesses so far, but I'll ask it again. Would the documents -- are they capable of informing you who gave the medication?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: And who was the co-signer?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: But you, as a band 5 nurse, were permitted to administer all medications; is that right?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: I couldn't administer them if they were going via central lines, but if they were going via IV lines I could -but I could check.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: Thank you. For the avoidance of any doubt, did [Baby M] have a central line?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: Did [Baby L] have a central line?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: Thank you. So medicines administered other than through a central line, you were permitted to do so?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: You are qualified to do so, I should say, more accurately.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: Thank you. But there would always be a co-signer --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Always, yes.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: -- for the administration of any medicine --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, most definitely.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: -- to any baby? And that applies to a baby in need of most intensive care in nursery 1 --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: -- is that right, or a feeder and a grower in nursery 4?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: Were nursery nurses qualified to administer medicine?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: They could check and administer vitamins and certain antibiotics, but beyond that, no.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: So if a baby in nursery 4, for example, required medicine, what would happen?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: The nursery nurse would alert us that they were due and then two members of the trained staff would draw it up, check it, check the baby and give it to the child.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: Thank you. As a matter of interest, would nursery nurses ever be given the keys to the medicine cupboard or refrigerator?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Not usually, no.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: Do you know why not?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Because of some of the drugs that were held within it.
blocks.speaker: GRIFFITH

blocks.text: Thank you. Let's go back to the carousel then, please, Mr Murphy. If we move across towards the [Baby M] event, we can see fluids being given to [Baby L] by you and your colleague Lucy Letby. Let's keep going across to see what else was happening.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: We have a further record of benzylpenicillin being provided by both of you to [Baby M], is that right, at 15.45?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: NURSE B: Yes.

blocks.text: NURSE B: Yes.

I'll ask this and by all means say if you do not recognise or are not sufficiently acquainted with it to recognise, whether you see Ms Letby's handwriting anywhere on the towel? blocks.text: NURSE B: I think it's possibly 16.23, but I can't be sure.

blocks.text: NURSE B: Yes.

blocks.text: There is a possibility.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Exactly, yes.

blocks.text: I know, yes. As I say, I'm not being critical, I'm just cautioning the jury at this stage that it's a difficult area.

(In the presence of the jury)
May I recall Dr Anthony Ukoh, please.

blocks.text: DR ANTHONY UKOH (recalled)
Examination-in-chief by MR DRIVER
Could you state your full name, please?
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: My name's Dr Anthony Ukoh.
blocks.speaker: UKOH

blocks.text: You understand that you're still under oath from your last visit to the witness box, which was last week, when you told us you were working at the Countess of Chester Hospital on a long day shift on Saturday, 9 April 2016?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Correct.
blocks.speaker: UKOH

blocks.text: Last week you gave evidence in relation to a patient, a twin, by the name of [Baby L]. This afternoon I'd like to ask you questions in relation to his twin brother, [Baby M]. I wonder whether Mr Murphy could put on screen tile 88 and the clinical note that lies behind it.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Firstly, Dr Ukoh, may I ask you, do you recognise this handwriting?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, that is my handwriting.
blocks.speaker: UKOH

blocks.text: Thank you. It is a note timed and dated at 10.25 on the morning of Saturday, 9 April. In what circumstances did you make this note?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: So this is a normal day in which we start with a ward round. So this is -- we've had a handover, which is normally done in the morning, between 8 and 9, and then after that, we then start to see the patients and then we make notes in this format.
blocks.speaker: UKOH

blocks.text: Thank you. Your note tells us that it was [Baby M]'s second day of life and the circumstances that presented in those first couple of days; is that correct?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: That is correct.
blocks.speaker: UKOH

blocks.text: Did you then undertake an examination of the baby at this time of this morning?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, I did. We normally for these ward rounds see the patient and examine them to make sure they're all well, yes.
blocks.speaker: UKOH

blocks.text: Thank you. What, if any, noteworthy entries are there on your note of the examination?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, so I'm just wondering if it can just come up a bit, sorry, further down. My entry there was saying that he looked well, he was settled and he was breathing okay.
blocks.speaker: UKOH

blocks.text: So there wasn't any major concerns I had. He was mildly jaundiced, but there wasn't any other -- he was on phototherapy light, which is what is used. Nothing unusual. There were no red flags at this point.
blocks.speaker: UKOH

blocks.text: Thank you. You made an examination of his abdomen, the note would suggest -- if we keep going down the page, Mr Murphy -- how was that at this point in time?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes. So from my earlier exam here, the abdomen was soft, it wasn't tender, so there wasn't any signs that he was in any pain, and I couldn't feel any masses. So it appeared like a normal exam at that point.
blocks.speaker: UKOH

blocks.text: Thank you. Then we move to your plan. Tell us the fourpoint plan, please.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes. The first one -- again, this is a BM check, which is just referencing blood sugars, which, because he was born slightly early and because he was a little bit low for weight, sugars were running slightly low. So it was just routine to check the sugars.
blocks.speaker: UKOH

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: The second entry there was to chase the (inaudible) on SBR, which is the jaundice level, because he was on the phototherapy lights.
blocks.speaker: UKOH

blocks.text: The third one there was for him to build up on feeds. At that point he would build up gradually to a certain amount.
blocks.speaker: UKOH

blocks.text: And then the fourth entry was us saying that if everything remains well, some of the blood tests -- if they come back clear, we'll then stop the antibiotics which we started, which was more of a preventative measure.
blocks.speaker: UKOH

blocks.text: Thank you. Could we go, please, to tile 149, Mr Murphy.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Click behind, please.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: My Lord, members of the jury, behind this tile now there are Dr Ukoh's note, which runs over a few of the clinical pages of the clinical notes. Extracts of it appear behind different tiles as
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: we go through the chronology of the carousel, but for ease of reference we've housed them all behind this tile so Dr Ukoh can go through it in a single sweep.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Thank you very much.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: So this suggests, does it, that you made the note at about 20.25 on 9 April?
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: Correct.
blocks.speaker: UKOH

blocks.text: But it was a note of events that occurred earlier in the day; is that correct?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: That's correct, yes.
blocks.speaker: UKOH

blocks.text: So made retrospectively at the earliest opportunity on a busy shift for events at approximately 16.02 hours.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: When you say approximately 16.02 hours, how were you able at 20.25 to note that time?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, because it was such a distinct event, it's not something that happens quite often, so I had an idea of what time it was and looking at certain recordings, something like that and then trying to piece things that happened -- yes.
blocks.speaker: UKOH

blocks.text: Thank you. So you noted retrospectively that at about that time, he, [Baby M], had a sudden and profound apnoeic episode. Were you present at the time of that episode?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, although I was covering both the general paediatric ward and also the special care, because although it's the same building, it wasn't in the actual same area, so yes, I happened to be on the actual unit when this happened.
blocks.speaker: UKOH

blocks.text: Thank you. What alerted you to an issue with [Baby M]?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: So it was -- I was called over by a very -- it was a frantic call to come over straightaway to this event.
blocks.speaker: UKOH

blocks.text: Even though I was there, I still had to find out at least what was happening.
blocks.speaker: UKOH

blocks.text: Yes. And so who reported the immediately preceding events or presentation to you?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: To be perfectly honest, I can't remember exactly who it was because at the time. This is all retrospectively, so I made these notes 2 years after, so I can't remember who it was. But I
blocks.speaker: UKOH

blocks.text: remember the event, I just can't remember who it was that actually called me.
blocks.speaker: UKOH

blocks.text: When you say you made the note 2 years after, do you mean you made your witness statement 2 years after?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Correct, yes.
blocks.speaker: UKOH

blocks.text: You made these notes at 20.25 on the day?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Exactly, yes.
blocks.speaker: UKOH

blocks.text: Thank you. You set out the chronology of this event and we can see about halfway down the page that you note:
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: "T-piece mask ventilation already in progress."
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Does that mean already in progress at the point of your arrival?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes. A call for help was put out. I was on the unit, I was in the room. So on my coming over, this has already been started, the CPR had already been started.
blocks.speaker: UKOH

blocks.text: Thank you.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Then we can see, looking at the left column, 16.02 hours, and then a line going into the body of the page. Could you read that to us, does it say, "Commenced"?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Sorry, is it all right for it to just come up a bit?
blocks.speaker: UKOH

blocks.text: Yes, please.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Which is the line, sorry?
blocks.speaker: UKOH

blocks.text: We've just noted that the T-piece mask ventilation was already in progress at your arrival and it's the next two lines that I'm asking to you help us understand.

blocks.speaker: UKOH

blocks.text: Thank you. We can see from your note that in addition to the cardiac massage, baby [Baby M] was administered a series of resuscitative medication; is that correct?
